# H7 — The subscriber-gated patterns bench (build-on-trigger work orders)

**Mission** — Hold nine pre-designed patterns at the ready without building any of them early. Each work order below is claimable only when its subscribe-when trigger has verifiably fired; when it fires, the team builds against the real subscriber's requirements under the junk gate, so every capability that lands has a consumer checking it against ground truth from day one. This is the north star applied to the kit's own roadmap: a pattern built without a subscriber is a claim with no evidence, and the bench exists to make that defect impossible.

**Repos & write scope** — Writes ONLY to `/Volumes/m2ext/code/geoffmilleraz/agentic-kit`. `../throughline`, `../sextant`, `../growing-gardens-bi` are READ-ONLY grounding (subscriber-side adoption is a hand-back item, never done from this repo's session).

**Trigger** — NOT ready now, by design. Each work order carries its own subscribe-when condition quoted verbatim from `docs/roadmap.md` (or `docs/plans/2026-07-uplift.md` §7 for WO-9). **Mandatory first step for any work order:** the coordinator records a new row in TRACKING.md's pull-queue table whose evidence field contains a **resolvable reference** — a commit SHA or repo-relative `file:line` in the subscriber repo naming the need (a vague friction-log sentence does not qualify; the row's existence and reference format are grep-checkable in the gate). That row then goes to Geoff for ratification (see hand-back) — **ratification is blocking: no implementer is dispatched before it lands**. A work order started without a ratified trigger row is out of scope and must be abandoned. Building two+ work orders in one wave requires two+ independently fired-and-ratified triggers — this spec makes that rule binding here; it is the pull-ordered *spirit* of uplift §2 amendment 2 ("no new zero-consumer package lands while a friction-log ask with a hand-rolled consumer implementation is open"), not a verbatim §2 rule, so cite this spec when enforcing it, not §2.

### WO-1 — Generalized context assembler (roadmap #2)
**Trigger:** "the first RAG-grade workload where 'what goes in the prompt' is a ranked decision, not a concatenation."
**Sketch:** New `foundations/prompt/context-assembler`: `Item{Kind, Priority, TokenCost, Content, Ref}` → `Assemble(items, budget, Options) (Assembly, error)`; `Options.Estimator func(string) int` matching `conversation.Options.Estimator` exactly (chars/4 default, documented error band); deterministic drop order (priority asc, then declared tiebreak); `Assembly.Dropped` lists every omitted item with reason — omission is always loud, mirroring `evidencecompactor`'s journal-before-drop stance. Graded chunks arrive via `truth-bridge` refs, never re-graded here. `context-renderer.Render` stays for prose; doc cross-links both. Assembled output enters the prompt via the **injection seam decision** (Design constraints) — NOT via `PreModelCall`, which cannot mutate.
- [ ] Package with schema.cue + testdata {symbol: Assemble, package: foundations/prompt/context-assembler}
- [ ] Harness integration test feeding `Assembly` output into the outbound request through the decided injection seam (pre-loop `Request`/`Config.Conversation` construction or the new mutating seam); a companion `PreModelCall` hook may *observe/veto* the assembled messages, nothing more
**Proof:** table-driven determinism test (same items+budget ⇒ byte-identical output, twice); dropped-item accounting test. **Theater trap:** a concatenator with a budget check is not an assembler — the ranked-decision test must show reordering under pressure, not just truncation.

### WO-2 — Cross-session agent memory (roadmap #3)
**Trigger:** "an assistant must remember across sessions ('what did we learn about X last week')." (TRACKING deferred row concurs: SQLite-backed Store is consumer-side.)
**Sketch:** `kits/memory` composing existing storage — no new stores: write policy interface defined over **foundation-level types** — `func(msgs []llmclient.Message) []Candidate` (or journal records), NOT over agent-harness's `RunResult`: kits compose foundations, and a kit→kit import of agent-harness is sanctioned nowhere — if the subscriber's shape genuinely demands it, the coordinator must get that dependency direction explicitly sanctioned via hand-back before building. Persistence = `jsonllog.Writer` episodic log + `vectorstore.Indexer` semantic index; consolidation emits `knowledgecardgeneration.KnowledgeCard` (archetype-validated, `aiprovenance` Author stamped) with `memorymanifest.Manifest` as receipt; decay via injected clock. Recalled memories enter the loop via the **injection seam decision** (Design constraints) — `HookConfig.PreModelCall` is observe/veto only and CANNOT inject; the candidates are pre-loop request construction, `Config.Conversation`, or a new optional `Deps.Memory` seam — decide against the subscriber's shape. Every recalled memory carries provenance; practices.md §15 (memory poisoning) binds: recalled content is untrusted input to the injection screen.
- [ ] Kit package, clock-injected, race-clean {symbol: New, package: kits/memory}
- [ ] Recall-into-request harness test through the decided seam; poisoned-memory canary test (planted injection is flagged)
**Proof:** round-trip test: run A writes, run B (fresh harness) recalls with provenance intact. **Theater trap:** a vector cache is not memory — without write policy, consolidation, and decay it's roadmap #3 unbuilt; and recall bypassing the injection screen is the §15 failure shipped.

## Design constraints

- Stdlib-only root module (empty require block, `constitution-lint` enforced); org-agnostic — no model IDs, provider catalogs, scope vocabularies, or company names as Go constants (model-catalog precedent: schema + loader, no shipped rows).
- **Injection seam (binding for WO-1/WO-2):** `HookConfig.PreModelCall` is observe/veto only and cannot mutate the outbound request. Assembled/recalled content enters via (a) pre-loop `Request`/`Config.Conversation` construction, or (b) a new mutating seam (optional `Deps.Memory` or a mutating hook variant) designed against the fired subscriber's shape. The coordinator decides (a) vs (b) at dispatch and records the decision in the TRACKING trigger row — teams must not burn a build rediscovering the hook signature.
- **Layering across kits:** foundations import stdlib + sibling foundations only; kits compose foundations. Kit→kit imports (e.g. kits/memory importing agent-harness types) are sanctioned nowhere — default to foundation-level types at kit boundaries; any kit→kit dependency requires explicit hand-back sanction recorded in TRACKING. WO-6's budget-guard work must stay WASM-safe (`GOOS=wasip1`).
- CUE owns shape: schema.cue + `testdata/*.cue` for every data-shaped package; behavioral-only packages may skip with the documented waiver.
- Injected clocks everywhere (`now func() time.Time` seam; nil-defaults documented); no sleeps, no network in tests; `-race` clean; concurrency contract in every package doc.
- Compose named seams, never wrap anew: `HookConfig`, `conversation.Options.Estimator`, `Pinger`/`ProbeAll`, `NewFailover` options, `ratelimiter.KeyedLimiter` shape, `llmtest.RunConformance` suite pattern, `hitl.Engine`. Extension interfaces over interface widening (`Pinger`/`ShreddableVault` precedent).
- Pull-ordered doctrine: check TRACKING pull queue before starting — open rows (D35-3/4/5) outrank any bench work order whose trigger hasn't fired.

## Acceptance = proof (machine-checkable only)

- Per fired work order: `task validate` green (fmt-check, vet, cue-vet, `go test -race ./...`); `constitution-lint` green; TRACKING.md row (trigger evidence with resolvable reference + capability checkboxes) and CHANGELOG.md entry in the same change; `task catalog` regenerated; `task downstream-check` with the run log captured as evidence showing **which consumers actually built** — skip-if-absent means an empty machine passes trivially, so a run where all siblings skipped does not satisfy this check; either run where the siblings exist or record the built-consumer list.
- The WO's own hard proofs as listed inline (canaries, conformance suites, API-shape tests, call-count assertions, exact-count greps).
- Anchors verified: `../sextant/bin/fathom verify --service agentic-kit --plan docs/plans/handoff-h7-patterns-bench.md` exit 0 (2026-07-16: corrected path — the file has never lived at `docs/plans/h7-patterns-bench.md`; that path was always wrong) — the `test_reaches` bug is fixed (H1, 2026-07-08), so this is the default verification path now; hand-verify via fathom `find_symbol` only on the O9 residue (aliased test calls, re-ambiguated methods), noted in the commit body if it applies. All unfired WO checkboxes remain `[ ]` — see the pre-push-gate note in Current state.
- Bench acceptance (no trigger fired): the spec file lands and is registered in `docs/plans/handoff-h0-index.md`, TRACKING pointer row exists, roadmap #14 "kit-side done" annotation lands (grep-verified phrasing), gate green — nothing else built, every WO checkbox still `[ ]`. **As of this revision, the roadmap #14 annotation has not landed** (dated note above) — this line of acceptance remains open.

## Non-goals & theater traps

- Do NOT build any work order whose trigger row isn't recorded and ratified — that is the exact "zero-consumer sprawl" headline finding #6 this bench exists to prevent.
- Do NOT re-spec graduated roadmap items (#1, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25). #14 is kit-side done, pending honest annotation — not "Graduated" until a consumer is named. Do NOT build eval-runner batch execution under WO-4's banner (that's roadmap #5's remaining half, separate trigger) or worker-pool execution (D7 owns it).
- Do NOT add persistent vector backends, a second cassette system, a fourth LLM routing wrapper, or an auto-applying improvement loop.
- Bench-wide theater trap: marking a roadmap entry "✅ Graduated" when only the kit-side shape landed without the subscriber consuming it — graduation requires the consumer wired (D2: composition proven, not asserted); the honest intermediate state is "kit-side done".
